reconstructed_theorem_text:
Fix a positive integer n, a nonnegative integer h, and an integer i with 0 <= i <= h. Write [d] = {0, ..., d-1}, set K = 2^(64(h+1)) and M = 2^(74(h+1)), and let P be the set of even integers p with 4 <= p <= K. For every k in [h+1] let m_k = h-k+1, and for p in P let T_(k,p) consist of the triples (r,j,l) with r in [p], j in [m_k], and l in [M^j]. Let C_(k,p) be the set of all functions from T_(k,p) to [n]. Take a standard Gaussian vector Xi in the real Euclidean space with coordinates (k,p,c), where k is in [h+1], p is in P, and c is in C_(k,p). Thus all entries Xi_(k,p,c) are independent standard normal variables.

Fix any deterministic family (u_j)_(j in [m_i]) of vectors in R^[n] with ||u_j||_2 = 1 for each j. Set S = sum_(j in [m_i]) M^j and, for p in P, set
a(p) = 1 / (p^4 S^2 sqrt(m_i log(2 K S))),
where log denotes the natural logarithm. Define the real-valued map
F(Xi) = sqrt(n) sum_(p in P) a(p) sum_(c in C_(i,p)) Xi_(i,p,c) prod_((r,j,l) in T_(i,p)) u_j(c(r,j,l)).

Then F is almost everywhere measurable under the standard Gaussian coefficient law, and its pushforward law is the real Gaussian with mean 0 and variance n sum_(p in P) a(p)^2. The nonnegative conversion on the variance leaves this expression unchanged. The assertion is for each fixed i and fixed unit-vector family; it gives no simultaneous bound over vector families and no law for a family chosen as a function of Xi. It does not assert that two evaluations using the same coefficient array are independent.
objects: A full standard Gaussian coefficient vector Xi, a fixed family of unit vectors u_j, the weights a(p), and the scalar F obtained by summing the selected level's weighted block evaluations. In each product over slots (r,j,l), the factor uses u_j at coordinate c(r,j,l).
domains: n is a positive integer, h is a nonnegative integer, i and the block level k belong to [h+1], and p belongs to the even integers in the inclusive interval [4, K]. Here [d] = {0,...,d-1}. At level k and degree p, slots are triples (r,j,l) in [p] x (disjoint union over j in [h-k+1] of [M^j]); c ranges over every function from these slots to [n]. The coefficient space is indexed by the disjoint union of all C_(k,p), and each u_j belongs to R^[n].
quantifiers: For all n, h, i, and all families (u_j) indexed by [h-i+1], if every u_j has Euclidean norm one, the stated law holds when Xi is drawn from the prescribed coefficient distribution. The sums and products are over all indicated finite indices.
assumptions: The displayed integer bounds, even degree restriction, and Euclidean unit norms hold. The vector family is fixed for the law assertion; Xi alone is drawn from the centered identity-covariance Gaussian on the entire coefficient space.
conclusion: F is almost everywhere measurable for the standard Gaussian measure and has pushforward distribution Gaussian(mean 0, variance n sum_(p in P) a(p)^2). The variance in the formal law is converted to a nonnegative real, without changing its value.
scopes: The input array contains blocks for every k and p; the evaluation at i uses only the distinct (i,p) blocks and ranges over all permitted p. The same u_j is used at every slot with that j. This is a marginal law for fixed parameters, not a simultaneous bound over all u, a guarantee for coefficient-dependent u, or an assertion of independence for arbitrary repeated evaluations on the same coefficients.
constant_dependencies: K = 2^(64(h+1)) and M = 2^(74(h+1)) depend only on h. m_k = h-k+1; level k has M^j slots at scale j for each of p copies. At the selected level m_i = h-i+1 and S = sum_(j=0)^(h-i) M^j. The weights are a(p) = 1/(p^4 S^2 sqrt(m_i log(2 K S))) with natural logarithm; they depend on h, i, and p. F has the prefactor sqrt(n), and the variance has prefactor n.
